# Glossary {#sec-glossary .unnumbered}

This glossary defines key terms used throughout *Physical AI*. Terms are organized alphabetically.

## A {#sec-glossary-vol4-a .unlisted}

**Action Chunk Seam Discontinuity**
: A mismatch in position, velocity, or acceleration where one admitted action chunk meets the next. An ideal velocity step implies an acceleration impulse; a finite acceleration step requests a finite torque step whose plant response depends on inertia and drive limits. The worked bridge matches position, velocity, and acceleration at its entry and reserves a separately admitted stop. (@Sec-planning)

**Astronomical Exposure Wall (Butler & Finelli Bound)**
: Under a stationary Poisson model, zero observed system-harm events require about $-\ln(0.05)/10^{-9}\approx3.0\times10^9$ independent failure-free machine-hours to place a one-sided 95% upper rate below $10^{-9}/\text{h}$. Aggregate exposure is possible, but is impractical within the illustrated fleet and policy-update interval; the bound says nothing by itself about unshielded hazardous-proposal rate or detector coverage. (@Sec-evaluation, @sec-verification, @sec-frontier)

## B {#sec-glossary-vol4-b .unlisted}

**Belief State Invalidation Horizon ($t_{\text{exp}}$)**
: The time at which a physical estimate no longer meets its declared error tolerance. A worst-case deadline requires a justified bounded-disturbance growth law; a calibrated quantile instead carries an explicit tail risk. Each cell or entity retains its own evidence epoch, independent of map publication time. (@Sec-memory)

## C {#sec-glossary-vol4-c .unlisted}

**Category 0 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**
: A stop by immediate removal of power to machine actuators. It is uncontrolled after removal: a moving motor may coast under safe torque off. Any mechanical brake is a separate, validated component; Category 0 is selected only when its coast and load behavior suit the hazard. (@Sec-enforcement)

**Category 1 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**
: A controlled stop with power available during deceleration, followed by removal of power after stopping. Its response and stopping distance depend on the implemented drive, brake, load, and monitoring path. (@Sec-enforcement)

**Category 2 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**
: A controlled stop with power retained after the stop, for example to maintain a verified powered hold. Continued power does not itself establish that a suspended or moving load is safe. (@Sec-enforcement)

**Causal Boundary**
: The transition from an independently admitted digital command to physical actuation. Subsequent energy transfer or contact can have irreversible effects even when software state is rolled back. The exact register, drive, and force timing are device-specific. (@Sec-boundary)

**Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE)**
: A safety-case structure linking a claim to a reasoned warrant and supporting evidence. Evidence can include analysis, qualified tests, field observations, and fault injection, with assumptions and residuals explicit; a fault log alone is not a release verdict. (@Sec-release)

**Covariate Shift Flywheel**
: In imitation learning, policy errors can move the robot to states underrepresented in demonstrations, where further errors become more likely. A quadratic-horizon behavioral-cloning bound requires the stated error, state-distribution, and cost assumptions; it is not a claim that every deviation reaches a hazard. (@Sec-data, @sec-training)

## D {#sec-glossary-vol4-d .unlisted}

**Demonstration Provenance Tuple**
: The 4-stream action logging protocol $(a_{\text{req}}, a_{\text{cmd}}, a_{\text{enf}}, a_{\text{meas}})$ that distinguishes intentional human teleop commands ($a_{\text{req}}$) from kinematic transformations ($a_{\text{cmd}}$), safety governor clamps ($a_{\text{enf}}$), and structural compliance/backlash ($a_{\text{meas}}$). (@Sec-data)

**Detectorless Failure Mode**
: A hazard mechanism for which the installed sensors provide no timely distinguishing signal before the required intervention deadline. Passive protection, operating restriction, or inspection may support a narrower claim when software detection cannot. (@Sec-frontier)

**Dynamic Fallback Ladder (MRM)**
: A menu of supervisor-owned responses such as command filtering, powered hold, controlled braking, and torque inhibit. The response is chosen from the current state and validated plant capability; these are not universally ordered by safety or latency, and torque inhibit can leave a moving load coasting. (@Sec-enforcement, @sec-intervention)

**Dynamic Stopping Distance ($d_{\text{stop}}$)**
: A conservative path-clearance bound combining pre-brake travel, braking travel under a validated lower bound $a_{\text{floor}}>0$ on achieved deceleration, and state/tracking allowance: $d_{\text{stop,bound}}=v\tau_{\text{pre}}+v^2/(2a_{\text{floor}})+\epsilon_d$ under constant speed before brake onset. Unknown braking capability does not support a positive speed permission. (@Sec-body, @sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-systems-stopping)

## E {#sec-glossary-vol4-e .unlisted}

**Endogenous Sensory Distribution Shift**
: Closed-loop actions alter the states the machine later observes, so deployed observations can depart from the demonstration distribution. A quadratic-horizon imitation bound holds only under its specified per-step error and downstream-cost assumptions. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-data, @sec-training)

**Envelope Trichotomy**
: Runtime evidence can support a claim as known true within a signed operating envelope, show it known false, or leave it unknown. Known false and unknown both refuse nominal tracking, but remain distinct records; the MCU chooses only a separately validated state-matched fallback. (@Sec-release)

**Expiring Intent Lease**
: A time-bounded request for tracking a grounded target under stated tolerance and evidence assumptions. The independent MCU checks the request and its own deadline. At expiry it withdraws tracking permission and uses the admitted fallback; physical stopping may finish after the tracking lease expires if that fallback has separate authority and reserved clearance. (@Sec-intent, @sec-planning)

## F {#sec-glossary-vol4-f .unlisted}

**Frozen Transform Trap**
: A transport bridge republishes an old spatial transform with a new publication timestamp. The capture or evidence epoch must remain attached so downstream age checks do not mistake stale geometry for a fresh observation. (@Sec-memory)

## I {#sec-glossary-vol4-i .unlisted}

**Inevitable Collision State (ICS)**
: A state from which no admissible control can avoid collision under the specified dynamics, actuator, obstacle-motion, and delay bounds. An ICS claim is conditional on that model and the available stopping or evasive actions. (@Sec-body, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement)

## L {#sec-glossary-vol4-l .unlisted}

**Lock-Free Seqlock Buffer**
: A single-writer shared-memory publication protocol using an odd sequence value during mutation and an even value after publication. The real-time reader makes one bounded copy attempt, accepts only matching even values plus integrity/freshness checks, and otherwise retains a validated command only within its lease before fallback. Coherent memory or explicit cache maintenance is also required. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-placement)

## M {#sec-glossary-vol4-m .unlisted}

**Minimal-Intervention Safety Shield**
: An independent filter that tests each candidate command against a feasible input constraint derived from a validated barrier and plant model. A candidate can violate the derivative constraint while the state still has $h(x)\ge0$; the filter then modifies or refuses it. A QP minimizes the selected command-space deviation, subject to actuator and timing limits, but does not by itself prove a Cartesian path safe. The $1\,\text{kHz}$ loop is an illustrative implementation. (@Sec-enforcement)

**Multidimensional Sim-to-Real Reality Gap Vector ($\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{\text{gap}}$)**
: A record of dynamics, sensing, appearance, and latency differences between a model and its physical plant. Its components have distinct units and can be combined into one score only after a stated normalization and risk rule. (@Sec-training)

## O {#sec-glossary-vol4-o .unlisted}

**Observational Indistinguishability Limit**
: Two world states generate the same available sensor record until the intervention deadline, so no downstream computation can choose different actions from that record alone. A common conservative response or passive bound may still protect both states if its force, timing, and actuator premises are validated. (@Sec-frontier)

## P {#sec-glossary-vol4-p .unlisted}

**Physical AI System**
: A system with learned live perception or policy whose admitted actions change physical state and later observations, and whose accepted proposals may actuate without case-by-case human approval. An independent veto can retain final permission authority while the machine still exercises delegated physical agency. (@Sec-boundary)

**Proposal–Permission Privilege Boundary**
: The separation in which a learned or other upstream controller proposes an action and an independent path retains authority to admit, modify, or refuse actuation under declared state and timing bounds. An MCU checking each millisecond is the worked example, not a universal implementation rate. (@Sec-boundary, @sec-brain, @sec-enforcement)

## R {#sec-glossary-vol4-r .unlisted}

**Residual-Claims Register**
: An auditable record of claims whose evidence or sensor coverage remains incomplete, naming the hazard, operating restriction or passive protection, evidence needed, and accountable owner. Inspection supports the evidence for a separately enforced restriction; it does not itself stop motion between checks. (@Sec-frontier)

## S {#sec-glossary-vol4-s .unlisted}

**Spatial Information Age ($\tau_{\text{age}}$)**
: Elapsed time between a spatial record’s capture or evidence epoch and the query or permission decision, after converting both clocks into one domain with bounded error. A full sensing-to-force response budget is a separate sum of detection, computation, communication, and actuator delays. (@Sec-perception, @sec-memory)

## T {#sec-glossary-vol4-t .unlisted}

**Two-Speed Embodied Compute Architecture**
: An illustrative partition between slower proposal generation and a bounded local permission and control path. The required rates follow the plant and hazard deadlines; the volume’s $1\,\text{kHz}$ MCU and slower model rates are examples. (@Sec-brain, @sec-placement)

## V {#sec-glossary-vol4-v .unlisted}

**Volumetric Free-Space Raycasting**
: Using a sensor ray to mark traversed cells before an observed hit as free in an occupancy layer, subject to range and occlusion validity. Near-surface TSDF fusion is a separate update; space behind the hit remains unknown unless observed from another ray. (@Sec-memory)

## W {#sec-glossary-vol4-w .unlisted}

**Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET)**
: A justified upper bound $C$ on a specified task’s execution on its target hardware and workload envelope. Response time runs from job release to completion and may include blocking, preemption, bus interference, and dispatch. Release jitter relative to a physical event must be handled separately when bounding event-to-actuation latency; $C$ alone is not that deadline. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-placement, @sec-appendix-systems-timers)

## Z {#sec-glossary-vol4-z .unlisted}

**Zero-Allocation SRAM Invariant**
: A design rule used by a particular real-time safety path to avoid unbounded heap work: required buffers and solver workspaces are preallocated in qualified local memory. Static allocation improves timing analyzability but does not by itself bound bus access, execution, or physical response. (@Sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement)
